- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67) or volatile (alternating ±0.67), model often underestimates upward momentum; add 1–3% to forecast if price is trending up.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If 3+ consecutive days of downward price movement, model tends to underestimate the depth of decline; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next period if sentiment is negative.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in high-volatility periods; if sentiment is mixed or neutral, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for reversion to prior mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period momentum; if sentiment turns positive after day 15–20, increase forecast by 1–2% for final 10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” oscillations (e.g., 0.67 → -0.67 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment swing direction.
